# Verdict: REVISE ## Summary The decision to retain focus in the search input while results update is sound and aligns with modern search interaction design. However, the component suffers from an **architectural pattern clash**: it mixes the semantics of an ARIA **combobox / listbox** with the DOM and keyboard behavior of a **list of navigation links**. Specifically: 1. `role="listbox"` with `role="option"` containing interactive `` elements violates WAI-ARIA rules (options cannot contain interactive children) and fails to implement `aria-activedescendant` or selection state. 2. The `` has `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-expanded`, but lacks `role="combobox"`. 3. The custom focus outline on result links fails WCAG 2.4.7 / 2.4.13 contrast requirements. 4. Loading states and "no results" announcements have communication gaps for assistive technologies. --- ## Pre-commitment Predictions - **Prediction 1**: Mismatch between `role="listbox"` / `role="option"` and interactive `` navigation links. (*Confirmed*) - **Prediction 2**: Missing `role="combobox"` on the search input despite combobox ARIA attributes (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete`). (*Confirmed*) - **Prediction 3**: Focus outline styling on result links removed or failing contrast. (*Confirmed: `outline: none` with light background change fails 3:1 contrast*). - **Prediction 4**: Missing loading/searching announcement for screen readers during network latency. (*Confirmed*). - **Prediction 5**: Incomplete keyboard navigation (missing Home/End, looping, or Enter key handling). (*Confirmed*). --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings (Blocks Access) 1. **Invalid ARIA Hierarchy: Interactive links nested inside `role="option"`** - **Location**: `LiveSearch.jsx:133-142` - **Impacted User Group**: Screen Reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA 1.2 Specification (Roles: `option`), WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) - **Why this matters**: Per the WAI-ARIA specification, elements with `role="option"` have `Children Presentational: true`. Interactive descendants (like ``) inside an `option` are disallowed and ignored by assistive technology trees, or cause conflicting accessibility tree calculations. Screen reader virtual navigation or listbox reading modes will announce these as options (expecting selection), but will fail to present them as operable links or read their destinations. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: Either: - **Option A (Recommended: Semantic HTML Navigation List)**: Remove `role="listbox"` and `role="option"`. Use a semantic `
    ` containing `
  • ...
    • `. Remove `aria-autocomplete="list"` from the input and use standard link navigation. - **Option B (True Combobox Pattern)**: Implement WAI-ARIA APG Combobox with `aria-activedescendant`. Move focus management to virtual focus (`aria-activedescendant` pointing to option IDs), keep physical focus on ``, and navigate to the URL on Enter. --- ### Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) 1. **Input Missing `role="combobox"` While Declaring Combobox Attributes** - **Location**: `LiveSearch.jsx:106-118` - **Impacted User Group**: Screen Reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA 1.2 Combobox Pattern; WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) - **Why this matters**: The `` has `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls="search-results-list"`, and `aria-expanded={results.length > 0}`, but lacks `role="combobox"`. In WAI-ARIA, `aria-expanded` and `aria-autocomplete` on a search input without a combobox role are unsupported or invalid on generic native inputs. Assistive technologies will not announce to the user that a popup list is available or expanded. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: If keeping the combobox model, add `role="combobox"` to the ``. If adopting a standard search + live results list, remove `aria-expanded` and `aria-autocomplete` and rely on `aria-describedby` / `role="status"` live announcements. 2. **Non-Compliant Focus Indicator on Results (`outline: none`)** - **Location**: CSS `ul[role="listbox"] a:focus` (line 54-58 in CSS) - **Impacted User Group**: Keyboard-only users, Low Vision users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible), WCAG 2.4.13 (Focus Appearance) - **Why this matters**: `outline: none` strips the browser's default focus ring. The replacement style is `background: #eff6ff` (very faint light blue) with `color: #1d4ed8`. Against the white menu background (`#fff`), `#eff6ff` has a contrast ratio of only **1.09:1**, far below the required **3:1** perimeter contrast ratio required by WCAG 2.4.13. Keyboard users navigating results cannot clearly perceive which item is focused. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: Keep a high-contrast outline on `:focus`: ```css ul a:focus { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: -2px; background: #eff6ff; color: #1d4ed8; } ``` 3. **`role="status"` Live Region Mounting / Timing Quirks** - **Location**: `LiveSearch.jsx:120-131` - **Impacted User Group**: Screen Reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) - **Why this matters**: The live region container combines both `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"`. When `resultCount === 0`, it renders `'No results found'`, which works. However, when the user is actively typing and the search is debounced/in flight, there is no announcement that searching has started (e.g. `aria-busy="true"`). Furthermore, clearing the search with Escape clears `resultCount` to `null`, creating an empty live region without confirmation that results were cleared. - **Confidence**: MEDIUM - **Fix**: Keep the live region persistently in the DOM (already done), set `aria-busy={isLoading}` on the search container or input, and announce state changes reliably. --- ### Minor Findings (Friction but Workaround Exists) 1. **Incomplete Keyboard Navigation Model in Results List** - **Location**: `LiveSearch.jsx:70-94` - **Impacted User Group**: Keyboard-only users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA Keyboard Navigation Practices, WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) - **Why this matters**: - Pressing `Home` or `End` while in the results list does not jump to the first/last item. - Pressing `ArrowDown` on the last item does not wrap or provide feedback. - Pressing `Tab` from inside the results list follows DOM order; if focus is on result 2, pressing `Shift+Tab` moves focus to result 1, but pressing `Tab` leaves the component entirely rather than cycling or moving predictably. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: Standardize list navigation keys (support `Home`, `End`, and wrap or stop predictably). 2. **Missing Form Landmark Context** - **Location**: `LiveSearch.jsx:101` - **Impacted User Group**: Screen Reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) - **Why this matters**: The search input is wrapped in a generic `
    ` rather than `` or `
    `. Search landmarks allow users to jump straight to site search via landmark navigation keys. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: Wrap the component in `` (HTML5.2 / native element) or ``. --- ## What's Missing - **Search Landmark**: Missing `` or `` wrapper. - **Loading State Indicator**: No `aria-busy="true"` on the input during network/debounce latency; screen reader users experience a silent delay before results arrive. - **High-Contrast Mode Support**: Transparent or subtle focus indicators break in Windows High Contrast Mode without an explicit `outline`. - **Keyboard Shortcut Hinting**: Sighted and screen reader users are not informed that Down Arrow moves into the result list. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |---|---|---| | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | `role="option"` wrapping ``, missing `role="combobox"` on input. | | **Keyboard-only** | **MEDIUM** | Focus outline removed on results (`outline: none`), faint background change. | | **Low vision** | **MEDIUM** | Result focus indicator contrast is 1.09:1 (fails 3:1). | | **Cognitive** | **LOW** | Clear visual hierarchy, simple search paradigm. | | **Vestibular & motion** | **LOW** | No motion/animations involved. | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No audio elements. | | **Environmental contrast** | **MEDIUM** | Needs high-contrast focus indicator border. | - **Screen Reader User**: Hear conflicting information. If VoiceOver/JAWS enters listbox mode, it expects options to be selectable via Space/Enter to populate the input, not to trigger page navigation. - **Keyboard-Only User**: Moving down into results loses clear focus distinction due to `outline: none` and faint background contrast. - **Low Vision User**: High ambient glare will render the focused result item completely invisible. --- ## Verdict Justification The design intention (keeping focus in the input while typing, using Down Arrow to enter results, announcing result count via live region) is **correct and recommended**. However, the implementation is marked **REVISE** because it conflates two incompatible ARIA patterns: 1. **WAI-ARIA APG Combobox / Listbox** (where items are `role="option"`, not links, and focus is managed via `aria-activedescendant`). 2. **Predictive Search Navigation Menu** (where results are an HTML list of anchor links ``). ### Recommended Remediation (The Cleanest Fix) Convert the component to a **Search Landmark with Navigation Results List**: 1. Change wrapper `
    ` to ``. 2. On ``: remove `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-expanded`; keep `aria-controls` or use `aria-describedby` pointing to the status announcement. 3. On `
      `: remove `role="listbox"`, use standard `
        ` with `
      • `. 4. On `
      • `: remove `role="option"`. Keep `` tags. 5. In CSS: restore `outline: 2px solid #2563eb` on `ul a:focus`.
